LEDGERLIB-104 (allocate_cents): I've hit a contradiction in the acceptance tests. Both test_largest_remainder and test_regression_issue_129 call allocate_cents(2, [1,1,1]) but expect different results: [1,1,0] vs [0,1,1]. A deterministic function can't pass both. The docstring says 'on equal remainders the earlier line wins' (=> [1,1,0]). Which behavior is the agreed design decision? @pavel @zoe

LEDGERLIB-114 (apply_discounts): my acceptance tests are self-contradictory. test_stacked expects apply_discounts(10000,['5.00','10%'])==8500 (i.e. % applied to the ORIGINAL amount) but also apply_discounts(10000,['10%','10%'])==8100 (i.e. percentages applied SEQUENTIALLY to the running amount). Per the design note, an amount-only match is made when exactly one unmatched invoice has that amount (INV-000102=12000 is unique), so 'INV-000102' is correct and test_regression_issue_590 looks like a test bug. Who owns acceptance/test_reconcile_payments.py? Should I file a qa-team issue?
